spec.record: D-reveal — Row truncated-text reveal + hover treatment
spec.design_question: When a row's title/subtitle/excerpt truncates at the island's 520px width, what gesture reveals the full text and on what surface (OS tooltip vs styled in-island tooltip vs inline peek expansion) — given that plain row click is irrevocably Open-on-GitHub and must stay unambiguous?
spec.current_state: Row click = Open-on-GitHub via NSClickGestureRecognizer (IslandContentView.swift:447, :530-532 radar; :551, :614-616 pulse), the H3 action ceiling (RadarPresenter.swift:78-88). Truncation: title 13px medium byTruncatingTail (IslandContentView.swift:480-484), subtitle 11px monospaced-digit (:486-490), excerpt 11px inkTertiary (:493-499) — all single-line, compression-resistance low. The original 'inspector' today = a one-line comment excerpt hard-capped at 100 chars at enrichment time (RadarPresenter.swift:91-101 `excerpt(maxLength:100)`, wired RadarPipeline.swift:127) — the full comment body never reaches the row model. The ONLY full-text reveal is the OS tooltip: `toolTip = title\nsubtitle\nexcerpt` (IslandContentView.swift:456-457; pulse :557) — OS-delayed (~1.5s), unstyled, un-themed. Hover treatment: IslandClickableView base (HUDPanel.swift:58-109) fades `theme.hoverFill` in/out over 0.12s CA easeOut (HUDPanel.swift:97-103), pointing-hand cursor, Reduce-Motion collapses to instant swap (:92-95); GitHub theme hoverFill = white α0.06 (Theme.swift:119), Increase-Contrast multiplies alpha ×2.2 (Theme.swift:70). The fill rect hugs the row's content bounds — row stack pinned at zero insets (IslandContentView.swift:513-518), radius 6 continuous (:444), so fill width varies per row. Geometry: island width 520 (IslandContentView.swift:9), content insets 18px h / 16px v (:109-120), inter-row spacing 8 (:206), per-lane scroll cap 240px (IslandGeometry.swift:19), island corner radius 14 (HUDPanelController.swift:32), GitHub theme surface is SOLID #0D1117, border #30363D (Theme.swift:113-119). Height is reactive: fittingHeight() sizes to content with whole-row snap (IslandContentView.swift:136-153, :186-196). Critical implementation fact: every render tears down and rebuilds the content view (HUDPanelController.swift:274-338); only scroll offsets are stashed/restored across rebuilds (:291, :311, IslandContentView.swift:157-181) — any new per-row reveal STATE would be lost on a poll-driven rebuild unless stashed the same way. Panel can never become key (HUDPanel.swift:11-13), so there is no in-panel keyboard focus today; rows are exposed to VoiceOver as buttons whose label already carries full title+subtitle (IslandContentView.swift:452-454) and accessibilityPerformPress opens GitHub (:523-526). No animation exists anywhere except the sanctioned hover fade; present() resizes the panel instantly (HUDPanelController.swift:326-338).

variants.name: Quiet Hand — status quo hardened
variants.essence: The one-line excerpt IS the final inspector; keep the OS tooltip as the only reveal and spend the record's budget on making the hover treatment uniform and honest.
variants.spec: REVEAL: unchanged — OS tooltip (title\nsubtitle\nexcerpt) on truncated rows only: set toolTip ONLY when measured intrinsic width of title OR excerpt exceeds available width (today it is set unconditionally, IslandContentView.swift:456), so a tooltip never restates fully-visible text. HOVER TREATMENT (the actual change): (1) rows pin trailing to the lane's trailing edge so every hover fill is a uniform slab 484px wide (520 − 2×18); (2) row content gets internal padding 8px horizontal / 5px vertical inside the fill; inter-row stack spacing drops 8px → 0 (effective text-to-text rhythm 5+5=10px, was 8); (3) fill: background rgba(255,255,255,0.06), radius 6px continuous, transition background-color 120ms cubic-bezier(0.0,0.0,0.58,1.0) in AND out (CA easeOut, matching HUDPanel.swift:100-101); cursor: pointer; Reduce-Motion → 0ms; Increase-Contrast → rgba(255,255,255,0.132). (4) NO new motion, no new surface, no new gesture. Click anywhere on the row = Open-on-GitHub, unchanged. COLLAPSE: n/a (OS-owned). KEYBOARD: n/a — VoiceOver label already carries full title+subtitle; add excerpt to the a11y label (append '. <excerpt>') so the spoken row equals the tooltip content.
variants.doctrine_fit: Perfect on its face: zero new surfaces, zero new motion beyond the already-sanctioned 120ms hover fade (HUDPanel.swift:87-89 explicitly blesses it as 1:1-to-pointer motion), calm preserved, nothing fabricated, hover stays secondary. The truncated-only tooltip rule is a small honesty win.
variants.risks: The reveal stays effectively broken — the OS tooltip is ~1.5s-delayed, unstyled, and visually foreign to the themed island (native-feel pressure cuts both ways: an OS tooltip is native but reads as a different product). For a 2-second-glance trust tool, a 1.5s dwell per row to read a truncated title undermines the glance promise. This variant is a deliberate 'do nothing final' answer; if the user picks it, the inspector question is closed as 'the excerpt is enough, the click is the reveal.'
variants.mock_notes: Island: 520px wide, solid #0D1117 (GitHub theme has NO blur — brand palettes require solid surfaces per INTENT iter 28), 1px solid #30363D border, border-radius 14px, padding 16px 18px, box-shadow 0 10px 30px rgba(0,0,0,.55). Header row: 'Needs you' 11px/600 #7D8590 + count badge (height 16px, border-radius 8px, background #2F81F7, white 11px bold tabular-nums, padding 0 7px) + right-aligned gear/chevron glyphs 13px #7D8590 in 24×22 hover targets (radius 5). Rows: CSS grid '20px 1fr' column-gap 8px; icon 13px glyph #7D8590 centered in 20×18; title 13px/500 #E6EDF3, white-space:nowrap, overflow:hidden, text-overflow:ellipsis; subtitle 11px #7D8590 font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums; excerpt 11px #484F58; 1px between text lines. Variant delta: each row gets padding 5px 8px, border-radius 6px, margin 0 (rows abut), width 100%; .row:hover{background:rgba(255,255,255,0.06)} with transition background-color 120ms cubic-bezier(0,0,.58,1); cursor:pointer. Fake the OS tooltip with title= attribute (real browser tooltip = honest analog of NSView toolTip, delay included). Footer: 'GitHub inbox ↗' 11px #484F58. Lane: max-height 240px, overflow-y:auto, overlay-style scrollbar (scrollbar-width:thin). Sample rows: one long title that truncates ('Fix race in PollScheduler when expand fires during an in-flight tick and the coalescer supersedes…'), subtitle 'provi/githud · @alice · review requested · 2h', excerpt 'I think the guard in setNeedsRender needs to also check isVisible before scheduling — otherwise…'.

variants.name: Inline Peek — click-to-expand in flow
variants.essence: Rows whose text truncates grow a quiet trailing disclosure chevron; clicking IT (never the row) un-truncates the row in place — the inspector's final form is the row itself, expanded.
variants.spec: AFFORDANCE: trailing disclosure control rendered ONLY on rows where measured title OR excerpt intrinsic width > available width (never fake chrome). SF 'chevron.down' 11px semibold, ink #484F58 at rest, #7D8590 while the ROW is hovered; hit target 22×18px, own hover fill rgba(255,255,255,0.06) radius 5px, pointing hand. Row layout: [icon 20px] 8px [text stack, flex] 8px [chevron 22px], chevron top-aligned to the title line box. GESTURE: click on chevron toggles peek; plain click anywhere else on the row = Open-on-GitHub, byte-for-byte unchanged (two separate hit targets — zero temporal or spatial ambiguity). Option-click anywhere on the row also toggles peek (power path). EXPANDED STATE: title wraps to max 3 lines (13px/500, line-height 16px), subtitle to max 2 lines, excerpt to max 4 lines (11px, line-height 15px); chevron rotates 180° over 140ms. The excerpt reveals the full 100-char model string; its trailing '…' (RadarPresenter.swift:100) is honest — 'more on GitHub' is the click. Pulse rows: same, title ≤3 lines, subtitle ≤2. MOTION: row height (and therefore island fittingHeight → panel frame) animates 140ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1) (decelerate), driven by NSAnimationContext 0.14s in the real app; Reduce-Motion → instant; whole-row lane snap (IslandContentView.swift:186-196) recomputed after. COLLAPSE: chevron click again (now pointing up); ALL peeks reset when the island collapses to the pill (fresh expand opens clean); peeks SURVIVE data-driven rebuilds within one expanded session by stashing the set of expanded row ids (thread id / PR url) exactly like ScrollOffsets (HUDPanelController.swift:291-311) and restoring after present(). If a rebuilt row's changeKey changed (new comment), drop its peek — the content is new, re-truncate honestly. HOVER: adopt os-tooltip-hardened's uniform full-width fill spec verbatim (484px slab, padding 8/5, 120ms easeOut). OS tooltip: removed on rows that have the chevron (one reveal channel, not two). KEYBOARD/A11Y: row gains accessibilityCustomAction 'Show full text' / 'Hide full text' toggling the same state; VO label already speaks full text so parity holds today; a future in-island keyboard scheme maps Space→peek, Return→open on the focused row (the two-target split makes that mapping trivial).
variants.doctrine_fit: Motion maps 1:1 to a deliberate click (height ease + chevron rotation are the click's direct echo — sanctioned by the same reasoning as HUDPanel.swift:87-89). No overlay, no z-order, no new surface — ink-only chrome. Discoverable WITHOUT hover (chevron always visible on truncated rows), so no hover-as-primary. Survives the gray-swap law trivially (shape carries everything). Open-on-GitHub ceiling untouched: the peek reads, never acts.
variants.risks: Adds a visible glyph column to most rows (long PR titles truncate often at 520px) — a calm cost, mitigated by #484F58 ink and truncated-only rendering, but it is new standing chrome. Island height now changes on peek: a peek near the lane's 240px cap converts growth into in-lane scroll rather than island growth (fittingHeight caps it), which the user may read as inconsistent. Peek-state stash/restore across rebuilds is real engineering (a new ScrollOffsets-like channel through HUDPanelController). The 100-char excerpt cap means the peek can under-deliver ('expanded and it's barely longer') — honest but potentially anticlimactic; raising the cap is a separate enrichment decision.
variants.mock_notes: Base island CSS identical to os-tooltip-hardened mock. Add per truncated row: a right cell (grid '20px 1fr 22px', gaps 8px) containing an inline SVG chevron (11×11, stroke #484F58, stroke-width 2) in a 22×18 button, border-radius 5px; button:hover{background:rgba(255,255,255,.06)}. Peek behavior in JS: click on the button toggles .peek on the row; .peek .title{white-space:normal; display:-webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp:3; -webkit-box-orient:vertical} (same pattern, clamp 2, on subtitle; clamp 4 on excerpt); chevron{transition:transform 140ms cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1)} .peek chevron{transform:rotate(180deg)}. Animate height with CSS grid-template-rows 0fr→1fr trick or measured max-height transition 140ms cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1) — and transition the MOCK island container's height the same way so the reviewer feels the panel reflow. Row click (not button) should visibly 'open GitHub' (e.g. flash a fake status line) to prove the primary action is untouched; option-click row toggles peek (e.altKey). Include one row whose text does NOT truncate → no chevron (show the honesty rule). Respect prefers-reduced-motion: transition:none.

variants.name: Hold to Peek — transient Quick-Look card
variants.essence: Press-and-hold a row (350ms) to float a themed card with the full text over it; release dismisses — a quick click still opens GitHub, and the island carries zero standing chrome.
variants.spec: GESTURE: NSPressGestureRecognizer on the row, minimumPressDuration 350ms, allowableMovement 4px, coexisting with the click recognizer; when the press begins, the click is cancelled (gesture precedence delegate). Click released < 350ms → Open-on-GitHub exactly as today. Hold ≥ 350ms → peek card appears; RELEASE → card fades out and NO navigation fires. Strict peek-while-held: no sticky state, no dismiss logic, no click-away interaction. CARD: anchored over the row — x = 18px (island content inset), width 484px, top = row top − 8px, auto-flips to sit fully above the row if it would cross the island's bottom inset. Surface #161B22 (one elevation step above #0D1117), 1px solid #30363D, radius 10px continuous, padding 12px 14px, shadow 0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.5). Content stack: full title 13px/500 #E6EDF3 wrap ≤4 lines (line-height 17px); 4px gap; subtitle 11px #7D8590 tabular-nums, 1 line; 8px gap + 1px #30363D hairline + 8px gap when an excerpt exists; full excerpt 11.5px #E6EDF3 α0.92, line-height 1.45, wrap ≤5 lines. MOTION: in — opacity 0→1 and scale 0.98→1, 120ms cubic-bezier(0,0,0.58,1), transform-origin at the press point; out — opacity →0, 100ms linear; Reduce-Motion → instant both ways. Card is added to the island's content view (clipped by the 14px island mask), never a second NSWindow — focus-non-theft holds structurally. Only rows with truncated text OR an excerpt arm the press recognizer. A data rebuild mid-hold simply drops the card (rare; honest). HOVER: adopt os-tooltip-hardened's uniform fill spec verbatim. OS tooltip: removed (the hold replaces it). COLLAPSE: release = gone; island collapse also tears it down. KEYBOARD/A11Y: VO label already speaks full title+subtitle; append the excerpt to the a11y label for parity (the card itself is a sighted-pointer convenience, VO never needs it); future keyboard maps Space (hold) if in-island focus ever exists.
variants.doctrine_fit: Calmest standing state of the four — literally zero added chrome at rest. Motion maps 1:1 to a sustained deliberate press (stronger than hover). Transient by construction: the card cannot linger, so attention-non-theft is structural. Nothing fabricated — the card shows exactly the model's strings. No hover dependence at all.
variants.risks: Discoverability is near zero — an invisible gesture on a product with no onboarding surface; most users may never find it. It ambiguates the click at the temporal margin: a slow deliberate click (>350ms, common for cautious users) becomes a peek-and-dismiss instead of Open-on-GitHub — a 'lost click' trust papercut on the PRIMARY action, which is precisely what the record's constraint forbids; 350ms is a tuning knife-edge. Gesture-precedence plumbing on a non-key panel (where NSButton is already unreliable, HUDPanel.swift:113-115) is the fiddliest implementation of the four. Card briefly occludes neighboring rows.
variants.mock_notes: Base island CSS identical to os-tooltip-hardened mock. JS: on row pointerdown start a 350ms timer; if pointerup fires first → run the 'open GitHub' flash (primary action); if the timer fires → set held=true and show the card; on pointerup while held → hide card, suppress the open. Card: position:absolute; left:18px; width:484px; background:#161B22; border:1px solid #30363D; border-radius:10px; padding:12px 14px; box-shadow:0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,.5); z-index:10; transform-origin set from the pointerdown coords; @keyframes in{from{opacity:0;transform:scale(.98)}to{opacity:1;transform:scale(1)}} 120ms cubic-bezier(0,0,.58,1); fade-out 100ms then display:none. Island container position:relative; overflow:hidden (the 14px mask clips the card like the real island would). Content: title clamp 4 (13px/500 #E6EDF3, line-height 17px), subtitle 11px #7D8590, hairline div 1px #30363D, excerpt 11.5px rgba(230,237,243,.92) line-height 1.45 clamp 5. Demo both placements: a top row (card below-flush) and a bottom row (card flipped above). Add a caption in the mock instructing 'click = open · hold = peek' since the gesture is invisible. prefers-reduced-motion → no keyframes.

variants.name: Styled Dwell Tooltip — the OS tooltip, made ours
variants.essence: Keep the exact trigger semantics the row already has (hover dwell) but replace the foreign OS tooltip with a fast, themed, in-island tooltip shown only when text actually truncates.
variants.spec: TRIGGER: pointer dwells 600ms over a row whose title OR excerpt truncates (measured, never unconditional); fully-visible rows never tooltip. NO chaining: moving to an adjacent row requires its own full 600ms dwell (deliberately calmer than OS menus — sweeping the pointer down the list must not strobe tooltips). DISMISS: pointer exits the row → fade out 80ms; any click → hide instantly (the click proceeds to Open-on-GitHub untouched); scroll in the lane → hide instantly; island rebuild → gone. PLACEMENT: below the row, leading edge aligned to the row's TEXT column (icon column + 28px from island edge, i.e. x = 18+20+8 = 46px), 6px below the row's bottom edge; max width 440px; auto-flips above the row when within 120px of the island's bottom inset; rendered inside the island content view (clipped by the island mask, never a separate window). SURFACE: #161B22, 1px solid #30363D, radius 8px, padding 10px 12px, shadow 0 6px 18px rgba(0,0,0,0.45). CONTENT: full title 12px/500 #E6EDF3 wrap ≤3 lines (line-height 16px); 4px gap; subtitle 11px #7D8590 tabular-nums 1 line; 6px gap; full excerpt 11px #7D8590 line-height 1.4 wrap ≤3 lines. MOTION: in — opacity 0→1 + translateY(2px→0), 100ms cubic-bezier(0,0,0.58,1); out — opacity →0, 80ms; Reduce-Motion → instant. One tooltip alive at a time. HOVER FILL: adopt os-tooltip-hardened's uniform fill spec verbatim; the tooltip and fill share the same tracking area. OS toolTip property: removed (superseded). COLLAPSE: automatic (pointer-exit); no user-managed state anywhere. KEYBOARD/A11Y: pointer-only by nature — parity via appending the excerpt to the VO label; no keyboard path exists or is planned for this surface, which must be stated to the human session as a known ceiling.
variants.doctrine_fit: Strictly dominates the status quo on native-feel (themed, in-island) and honesty (truncated-only, faster than the OS delay so the glance promise holds). Motion is 1:1 with the pointer's dwell-and-leave, same sanction as the hover fade. Transient — no standing chrome, no state. Click is never touched.
variants.risks: It deepens the hover channel exactly where INTENT iter 1 flagged 'hover-as-primary' as a trap: reading full text becomes a hover-ONLY act, undiscoverable and unusable without a pointer, and unlike the chevron there is no visible affordance ever. Dwell tooltips popping during casual pointer travel is a mild attention-theft vector (mitigated by 600ms + no chaining, but nonzero). A custom tooltip view re-implements something the OS gives free — pure presentation code with clipping/flipping edge cases at the lane's scroll boundary (a tooltip for a half-scrolled row near the cap must clip or hide).
variants.mock_notes: Base island CSS identical to os-tooltip-hardened mock. JS: per truncated row, pointerenter starts a 600ms timer (cleared on pointerleave/click/scroll); on fire, inject the tooltip div positioned absolutely at left:46px, top = rowBottom+6 (or rowTop − tooltipHeight − 6 when flipping — demo one of each). Tooltip: max-width:440px; background:#161B22; border:1px solid #30363D; border-radius:8px; padding:10px 12px; box-shadow:0 6px 18px rgba(0,0,0,.45); animation in 100ms cubic-bezier(0,0,.58,1) {opacity:0→1; transform:translateY(2px)→0}; removal after an 80ms opacity fade. Title 12px/500 #E6EDF3 -webkit-line-clamp:3; subtitle 11px #7D8590 tabular-nums; excerpt 11px #7D8590 line-height 1.4 clamp 3. Island container position:relative; overflow:hidden. Show no-chaining honestly: moving to the next row must restart the 600ms dwell in the mock. Include one non-truncating row that never tooltips. prefers-reduced-motion → animation:none.

recommendation.why: It is the only variant where the reveal is discoverable without hover (a visible ink affordance, honoring the iter-1 hover-as-primary warning), gesture-unambiguous (a separate hit target — plain row click stays byte-for-byte Open-on-GitHub, unlike hold-to-peek's 350ms knife-edge), and in-flow with motion mapped 1:1 to a click. It also gives the original 'inspector' a principled final form — the row itself, expanded on demand — with the cleanest future keyboard/VoiceOver path (a toggle action beside the press action). Its real costs (chevron chrome on truncated rows, peek-state stash across rebuilds) are visible in the mock and honestly priced, whereas the tooltip variants hide their cost in undiscoverability.

review.record: D-reveal — Row truncated-text reveal + hover treatment

verdicts.reason: Doctrine-clean on every axis: zero new motion (only the already-sanctioned 120ms hover fade, which the code does animate both directions — verified HUDPanel.swift:90-104), zero new surface, no color, no fabrication; the truncated-only tooltip rule and the excerpt-appended VO label are honesty wins; Increase-Contrast math (0.06x2.2=0.132) matches Theme.swift:70 exactly. But the truncation predicate as specced ('title OR excerpt') is a regression against the status quo it claims to harden: the subtitle (repo · actor · reason, 11px, compression-resistance low, IslandContentView.swift:486-490) truncates readily at 484px, and a subtitle-only-truncated row would lose the tooltip it has today — the 'never restate visible text' rule accidentally becomes 'sometimes hide truncated text', which cuts against the never-miss ethos.
verdicts.amendment: Truncation predicate = measured intrinsic width of title OR subtitle OR excerpt exceeds available width. Nothing else changes.

verdicts.reason: Doctrinally the strongest reveal: discoverable without hover (honors the iter-1 hover-as-primary flag), motion strictly click-mapped with Reduce-Motion collapse (same sanction class as the hover fade), ink-only chrome, gray-swap trivial, Open-on-GitHub ceiling untouched, changeKey-based peek invalidation references a real concept (RadarPresenter.swift:154). But its central safety claim — 'two separate hit targets, zero ambiguity' — is FALSE against the current codebase: IslandClickableView.hitTest (HUDPanel.swift:65-67) deliberately flattens the entire row to one target so child views never swallow first-mouse clicks; a chevron child as specced can never receive its own click, and the failure direction is the worst one (peek attempt -> unwanted navigation, violating the record's own click-unambiguity constraint). Also under-specced: RadarRow carries no stable id (RadarPresenter.swift:6-18; url is optional and collides on the repo-page fallback :85-88) and changeKey lives on RankedThread not RadarRow, so the 'exactly like ScrollOffsets' stash actually requires a GithudCore model change. And it introduces the product's first panel-frame animation (present() is instant today) — sanctioned because click-mapped, but it must be named to the human session as a deliberate first, not smuggled in as precedent.
verdicts.amendment: (1) Spec the hit-target split against the real base class: override the row's flattening hitTest to carve out the chevron's frame, and give the chevron acceptsFirstMouse=true + mouseDownCanMoveWindow=false, with an explicit test that a chevron click NEVER navigates. (2) Add a stable row identity (thread id) plus a per-row change signature to RadarRow/PulseRow as the peek-stash key — do not key on optional/collidable url. (3) Truncation predicate includes subtitle. (4) Flag the panel-height animation to the human session as the first panel-frame motion in the product.

verdicts.reason: Violates the record's own binding constraint — 'plain row click is irrevocably Open-on-GitHub and must stay unambiguous' — which is the interaction-layer expression of the trust moat (INTENT: the existential axis is trust; a lost action erodes trust exactly like a missed mention). A press >=350ms followed by release silently swallows the product's ONE action: the user meant open, nothing happens, no feedback that the intent was reinterpreted. The variant's own risks section concedes this ('precisely what the record's constraint forbids') — it is self-refuting. No minimal amendment preserves the essence: navigate-on-release-after-hold double-fires the action; raising the threshold only relocates the knife-edge; the temporal split IS the variant. Secondary confirmations of the kill: discoverability requires the mock to carry an instruction caption ('click = open · hold = peek') — a teaching surface the shipped product does not have, so the mock demonstrates an affordance the real product cannot convey; and the gesture-precedence plumbing lands on exactly the non-key-panel terrain the codebase already documents as unreliable (HUDPanel.swift:111-113).

Not a kill: the reveal is a secondary convenience, not the primary interaction (click->GitHub is untouched, VO parity holds via the label), so the hover-as-primary trap — flagged at iter 1 against hover as the SUMMON — is skirted rather than sprung, and the spec honestly names the pointer-only ceiling. The 600ms no-chaining dwell is a real attention-theft mitigation, and departing from the OS tooltip is a preference-level native-feel departure with an explanation (1.5s delay defeats the 2-second-glance promise), which PRESSURE permits. But two doctrine burrs: (1) the entrance motion fires on TIMER EXPIRY, not on a pointer event — the sanctioned hover fade maps to enter/exit actions (HUDPanel.swift:87-89), whereas a dwell-pop is motion with no action instant and no real change behind it; the opacity fade is defensible as softened appearance (the OS tooltip's own class), but the translateY(2px) slide is pure decoration under the strict 1:1 law and must go. (2) Same shared predicate gap: subtitle truncation is omitted, so a subtitle-only-truncated row never tooltips even though the tooltip's own content includes the subtitle.
verdicts.amendment: (1) Entrance motion = opacity-only (<=100ms) or instant; delete the translateY — no positional motion on a timer-fired appearance. (2) Truncation predicate includes subtitle. (3) Keep the spec's own requirement that the pointer-only ceiling is stated verbatim to the human session — make it binding, not optional.

review.overall_note: Code verification: every load-bearing file:line claim in current_state checks out (click gestures, unconditional tooltip, 100-char excerpt cap with full body discarded at RadarPipeline.swift:127, teardown-rebuild render with only ScrollOffsets stashed, canBecomeKey=false, hover fade as the codebase's ONLY animation — grep-confirmed; sole drift: the NSButton comment is HUDPanel.swift:111-113 not :113-115, immaterial). Two facts the record missed change the picture for the human session: (1) IslandClickableView.hitTest (HUDPanel.swift:65-67) flattens each row to ONE hit target by design — the chevron variant's 'zero ambiguity' claim is false until that carve-out is specced, and the un-amended failure mode is a peek click that NAVIGATES, the worst possible violation of the record's own constraint; (2) RadarRow has no stable identity (no thread id; url optional + collidable on the repo fallback), so chevron's peek-stash needs a GithudCore model change, not just a view-layer stash. Shared defect across all three surviving variants: the truncation predicate omits the subtitle. On the recommendation: chevron-inline-peek is a defensible pick and the only variant that actually answers the design question without hover — but ONLY with the hitTest amendment made blocking; as written its central safety claim doesn't survive contact with the code. If the session wants the strictly doctrine-safest option, that is os-tooltip-hardened (zero new anything) at the honest price of closing the inspector question as 'the click is the reveal.' hold-to-peek-card should not reach the session: it is self-refuting (its own risks section admits violating the record's binding click-unambiguity constraint) and no minimal amendment preserves its essence.
